summary: B is preferable because it verifies the new API’s multipart payload and retry behavior end to end, whereas A’s retry test only exercises a generic bytes.Reader request. Both patches nevertheless violate an explicit contract requirement by duplicating Add’s request logic instead of calling FilesService.Add.
reasons: B’s Upload test checks the required field name, uploaded filename, and file contents; A does not verify the contents.

B directly proves that an Upload body survives a 429 retry and arrives intact on the second attempt. A only proves the already-generic fact that net/http makes a bytes.Reader replayable, without connecting that behavior to Upload.
B provides separate, clearer validation errors for an empty filename and nil content, while A collapses both cases into one ambiguous error.
B documents the distinction between the low-level Add API and the replayable convenience API, improving usability and preserving Add’s role.
risks_a: Upload directly duplicates Add’s option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing through Add as explicitly required.
Tests omit actual Upload retry coverage, uploaded-content verification, validation cases, and source-reader failure propagation.
The added retry transport test largely verifies net/http behavior for bytes.Reader rather than the requested FilesService behavior.
risks_b: Upload also directly duplicates Add’s implementation instead of delegating to Add, creating a maintenance divergence risk and violating the frozen contract.
Despite broader coverage, tests still omit required validation and source-reader error cases.

The extra Add non-replayable-body test and extensive documentation add some scope beyond the focused API change, and retry wording may be read as unconditional even though method retry policy still applies.
